subject: Request: temporary priority lane for Blackrock simulation (fairness-tier exception)
messages:
From: Jamie Lowe <jamie@snowcap.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@snowcap.ai
Date: 2026-05-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Priority lane request for May 22 smoke test

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Hope you’re both well. We’re running a full-stack simulation of our Blackrock integration on May 22–23 and expect a short-lived spike in request volume (~2–3M tokens/hour at peak, roughly 180 QPS sustained for 90 minutes). For the test to be meaningful we need consistent latency under 120ms P95 and would like to request a temporary priority lane (fairness-tier carveout) to avoid our traffic being throttled or deprioritized by fair-share policies.

Key asks:
- Temporary priority lane for 2026-05-22 18:00–2026-05-23 03:00 PDT
- Soft SLA: P95 latency < 120ms for the test window
- Guarantee no token-based throttling for the flagged routes during the window

We can provide load plan and sample traffic profiles (attached). We’re treating this as a pilot; if successful, it will be part of the SC-9821 deal. Please let us know the process and any required paperwork.

Thanks,
Jamie
Head of Integrations | Snowcap AI
jamie@snowcap.ai

Attachment: snowcap_loadplan.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lowe <jamie@snowcap.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority lane request for May 22 smoke test

Jamie — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the load plan. We can help, but need to confirm a few technical details before we commit to an exception window. Specifically:

1) Exact route(s) you want prioritized (endpoint paths or model IDs).
2) Average token length and token distribution per request (you noted ~2–3M tokens/hr; is that aggregate across 4 routes or concentrated?).
3) Would you accept a staged ramp (30m warmup @ 30% traffic, then ramp to peak)? Caching behavior (prefix reuse) matters for our batching heuristics.
4) Any compliance constraints we should be aware of for the test (PII, retention toggles)?

Operational asks from our side: if we approve a temporary priority lane we’ll require a signed addendum to the SLOs, an explicit MAPl (mutual action plan) for the runbook, and that you route traffic via the test route name we assign. Monica — can you draft a SLO addendum and a recommended ramp profile? Vivek — can you confirm capacity impact and whether we can offer a soft SLA for that window (target P95 <120ms) without affecting other customers?

Jamie — once you confirm points 1–3 we’ll fast-track the approval and share a DocuSign link for the addendum.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (650) 555-0142

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Priority lane request for May 22 smoke test — proposed SLO addendum

Team — I reviewed the loadplan and sketched a conservative approach. Points below and attached draft SLO addendum.

Summary of Snowcap ask (from attachment):
- Peak ~180 QPS for ~90 minutes; aggregate 2–3M tokens/hr
- Test window: 2026-05-22 18:00–2026-05-23 03:00 PDT

Proposed approach:
- Assign a temporary route tag: /routes/snowcap/blackrock-test
- Ramp plan: 30m warmup (30% traffic), 30m mid (60%), 30m to peak (100%), maintain for 90m, and 60m cool-down at 50%
- Token guardrail: disable per-route burst throttling for the tagged route only during the window; keep cluster-level fairness enabled with a soft carveout allocation of +12% capacity for the window
- Monitoring: SLO dashboard (latency, error-rate, token-usage) with alerting to on-call SRE and to the Snowcap point of contact

Risk/impact: Moderate — estimate transient P95 increase for adjacent tenants ~<5–8% given current cluster headroom; Vivek, please confirm capacity numbers.

Attached: slo-addendum-draft.pdf (contains the exact wording for the temporary carveout and the mutual action plan). Please review and suggest edits; once agreed we can send to Jamie for signature.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Platform Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: slo-addendum-draft.pdf

From: Jamie Lowe <jamie@snowcap.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@snowcap.ai
Date: 2026-05-19T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority lane request for May 22 smoke test

Thanks Rishi / Monica — this looks good and aligns with our internal test plan. Responses inline:

1) Routes: we’ll use two endpoints: POST /v1/infer/blackrock and POST /v1/infer/blackrock-batch (both mapping to model id rc-13b-prod).
2) Token distribution: median 160 tokens/request; 95th% ~420 tokens. The attached loadplan has the request mix.
3) Staged ramp is fine — we prefer aggressive ramp to reach peak earlier (can compromise on a slightly shorter warmup).

We reviewed the SLO addendum and procurement is ready to sign a short-term addendum for the window. Please send the DocuSign link and the exact route tag you’ll assign; we need those to configure our traffic generator.

Appreciate the quick turn.

—Jamie

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lowe <jamie@snowcap.ai>
